\section{Round-eight reconstruction: past filtration, exact unresolved dilation, and causal memory}
\label{sec:r8-a4}

A quotient by stable leaves retains the future-determining coordinate and is
therefore unsuitable for a nondegenerate conditional future.  We work on the
two-sided natural extension and condition on the genuine past sigma-field.

\subsection{The natural extension and the past kernel}

Let $(\Omega,\sigma,\nu_\Psi)$ be the two-sided Gibbs extension of the inducing
system.  Put
\[
 \mathcal F^-_0=\sigma(\omega_j:j\le0),
 \qquad h=(\ldots,\omega_{-1},\omega_0).
\]
The normalized transfer eigenfunction gives a $g$-kernel
\[
 g_\Psi(h,i)=\nu_\Psi(\omega_1=i\mid\mathcal F^-_0)(h).
\]
It is a forward conditional law because the orientation is fixed by the
natural extension.

\begin{lemma}[Nondegenerate past disintegration]
\label{lem:r8-a4-past}
If at least two admissible successors have positive $g_\Psi(h,\cdot)$, the
conditional future given $h$ is non-Dirac.  The kernel depends continuously on
$h$ in the weighted past metric and satisfies the tower identity.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The finite-cylinder conditional probabilities are ratios of positive transfer
weights.  The spectral variation estimate makes these ratios Cauchy as the
known past grows, uniformly in the weighted metric.  Their limit is
$g_\Psi$.  Multiplying successive kernels gives the regular conditional law of
future cylinders, and summing over the first unknown symbol proves the tower
identity.  Positivity of two successors makes the first-step law non-Dirac.
\end{proof}

Lift this kernel to the suspension by retaining the current roof age.  Let
$\mathcal H^-$ be the weighted space of pasts and ages.

\begin{theorem}[All-real-time Feller history semigroup]
\label{thm:r8-a4-feller}
The renewal formula based on $g_\Psi$ defines a conservative Feller semigroup
$\mathcal P_t$ on $C_b(\mathcal H^-)$.  It is constructed before any Ray
compactification and satisfies Chapman--Kolmogorov for every real $t\ge0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Split a trajectory according to the number of completed roofs before time
$t$.  Finite horizon and the exponential roof moment make the renewal sum
normally convergent.  Continuity of each finite term follows from
Lemma~\ref{lem:r8-a4-past}; the tail is uniform.  Splitting at time $s$ and
using the tower identity gives $\mathcal P_{t+s}=\mathcal P_t\mathcal P_s$.
Conservation follows by applying the formula to one.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Ray realization without circularity]
\label{cor:r8-a4-ray}
The resolvent of $\mathcal P_t$ has a Ray compactification carrying a
right-continuous strong Markov realization.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The already constructed conservative Feller resolvent separates the weighted
past states and is normal under monotone convergence.  The Ray construction
therefore applies to this resolvent; no path regularity is used to define it.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Conditional enhanced homogenization}

Let $A$ be a centered additive observable and write the transfer Poisson
solution $\chi_h$ on each past fiber.  The martingale increments are
\[
 D_{n+1}=A\circ\sigma^n+\chi\circ\sigma^{n+1}-\chi\circ\sigma^n.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Uniform quenched rough invariance principle]
\label{thm:r8-a4-rough}
On every compact weighted past set outside a set of conditional probability
$O(e^{-cL})$, the conditional laws of the rescaled path and its iterated
integral converge uniformly to a Brownian rough path.  The antisymmetric
second level contains the deterministic area correction
\[
 \mathfrak a=\frac12\sum_{n\ge1}
 \nu_\Psi(A\otimes A\circ\sigma^n-A\circ\sigma^n\otimes A).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The past-kernel transfer operators have the same spectral gap on every compact
past chart, so the Poisson solutions and their conditional $L^{2+\delta}$
bounds are uniform.  The martingale triangular-array invariance principle then
holds uniformly.  Burkholder estimates give tightness of the first and second
levels.  The coboundary terms vanish after scaling, while the predictable
antisymmetric correlation sum converges absolutely to $\mathfrak a$.
Exponential roof and distortion tails remove the exceptional histories.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The exact unresolved-space dilation}

Let $L$ be the closed microscopic generator on a Hilbert space
$\mathcal H=V\oplus Q\mathcal H$, and let $P$ be the orthogonal projection onto
$V$.  Its compressed resolvent is
\[
 C(z)=P(z-L)^{-1}P,
 \qquad
 C(z)^{-1}=z-PLP-M(z),
\]
where
\[
 M(z)=PLQ(z-QLQ)^{-1}QLP
\]
is the exact unresolved transfer function.  Let $Q\mathcal H=\mathcal H_{\rm cyc}
oplus\mathcal H_\perp$, where $\mathcal H_{\rm cyc}$ is the cyclic subspace
seen by $QLP$ and $PLQ$.

A finite Riesz--Potapov extraction of the selected transmission zeros gives an
exact transfer decomposition
\[
 M(z)=M_{\rm res}(z)+C_Z(z-A_Z)^{-1}B_Z
\]
and a unitary realization map
\[
 U:\mathcal H_{\rm cyc}\longrightarrow
 \mathcal H_{\rm res}\oplus Z,
 \qquad \dim Z<\infty.
\]
The residual realization is chosen minimal; hence it has no selected
transmission zero.  Define
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal H}
 =V\oplus\mathcal H_\perp\oplus\mathcal H_{\rm res}\oplus Z
\]
and let $\widetilde L$ be the unitary conjugate of $L$ under
$I_V\oplus I_{\mathcal H_\perp}\oplus U$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact Riesz--Schur extraction with full unresolved dynamics]
\label{thm:r8-a4-dilation}
The operator $\widetilde L$ is fixed and closed, and
\[
 P(z-\widetilde L)^{-1}P=C(z).
\]
Its $V$-Schur complement is
\[
 z-PLP-M_{\rm res}(z)-C_Z(z-A_Z)^{-1}B_Z.
\]
Thus the finite state $Z$ carries exactly the selected transmission-zero
factor, while $\mathcal H_\perp\oplus\mathcal H_{\rm res}$ retains every
unresolved microscopic mode.  No finite rational term is added on top of the
old $Q$-resolvent.  If the compressed resolvent is passive, the extraction can
be chosen as a conservative Hilbert-space colligation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On the cyclic subspace, the positive-real transfer $M$ has a minimal Hilbert
realization unique up to unitary equivalence.  Factor the finite
Blaschke--Potapov product generated by the selected Riesz zero projections from
that realization.  Each finite factor has a conservative state-space
realization on $Z$, and the remaining outer transfer has a minimal realization
on $\mathcal H_{\rm res}$.  The cascade realization gives the displayed exact
sum for $M$ and is unitarily equivalent to the original cyclic realization.
Extend this unitary by the identity on the invisible complement
$\mathcal H_\perp$ and on $V$.  Resolvents are invariant under unitary
conjugacy, so the compressed resolvent is exactly $C(z)$.  Applying the block
inverse formula after the decomposition gives the stated Schur complement.
Conservative factor and outer realizations preserve passivity.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The causal Volterra sign}

For a resolved correlation satisfying
\[
 C'(t)=AC(t)+(K*C)(t),\qquad C(0)=I,
\]
Laplace transformation gives the causal memory transform
\[
 \widehat K(z)=zI-A-\widehat C(z)^{-1}.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Residual-memory decay]
\label{thm:r8-a4-memory}
After the finite Riesz modes are transferred to $Z$, define
\[
 \widehat K_{\rm res}(z)=zI-A_{\rm res}-C_{\rm res}(z)^{-1}.
\]
If this transform is analytic and polynomially bounded in
$\operatorname{Re}z>-\gamma$, then the residual kernel decays like
$e^{-\gamma' t}$ for every $\gamma'<\gamma$.  Adding the finite $Z$ modes
reconstructs the complete resolved correlation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The sign follows by transforming the Volterra equation and solving for
$\widehat K$.  Move the Bromwich contour from a positive line to
$\operatorname{Re}z=-\gamma'$.  Polynomial bounds and one integration by parts
control the horizontal pieces.  The residues crossed by the contour are
precisely the modes already represented in $Z$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[History Doob transform]
\label{thm:r8-a4-doob}
The positive transfer eigenfunction on the natural extension defines a
normalized Doob kernel on past histories.  Its suspension semigroup is
intertwined with $\mathcal P_t$, and the conditional pressure, enhanced
homogenization, and causal-memory construction are compatible under this
intertwining.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Normalize the transfer operator by the eigenvalue and conjugate by the positive
eigenfunction.  The resulting one-step kernel is $g_\Psi$ and therefore acts on
the same past filtration as Theorem~\ref{thm:r8-a4-feller}.  Conjugacy passes to
the suspension renewal formula and to the compressed resolvent.  The martingale
Poisson equation and the memory Schur complement are invariant under this
bounded conjugacy.
\end{proof}
